--- title: "[Graph.add_star_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a star graph (hub-and-spoke) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6161-L6268){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_star_graph( n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Star graph](/assets/graphs/add-star-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three star graphs side by side: a hub with three spokes for n=4, four spokes for n=5, and six spokes for n=7. The hub is joined to every other node and the spokes are not joined to each other, so n nodes give n - 1 edges." width="100%"} Creates a central hub node connected to `n - 1` peripheral nodes. All edges connect the hub to spokes; there are no edges between spokes, so `n` nodes always give exactly `n - 1` edges. The hub is the first node created and the spokes follow it in order. In a directed graph every edge points outward, from the hub to a spoke. The new nodes are appended to whatever is already in the graph: nothing is cleared and no edges are made to existing nodes. Star graphs are handy for: - modeling hub-and-spoke systems (a server with clients, an airline hub, a broadcaster) - building test graphs with one extremely central node, e.g. to sanity-check centrality measures - assembling larger structures by attaching stars to existing nodes with `add_edge()` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes to add, counting the hub (so `n - 1` spokes). Must be at least `2`; smaller values raise a `ValueError`. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node, e.g. `"server"`. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string (so `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in an empty graph). The hub gets the first number. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge, e.g. `"connects"`. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `2`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star graph has one hub connected to every other node, with no edges between the spokes themselves -- so `n` nodes always produce exactly `n - 1` edges: ::: {#6ec48aaf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=5) # 1 hub + 4 spokes graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (5, 4) ``` ::: ::: Listing the edges shows that every one of them starts at the hub, node `"1"`: ::: {#52ba0b27 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1--2', '1--3', '1--4', '1--5'] ``` ::: ::: `type=` tags every new node (and `rel=` every new edge), so the node table gains a `type` column. Its degree column confirms that the hub has degree `3` and each spoke degree `1`: ::: {#ab18df3e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=4, type="server", rel="link") graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (4, 4)
idlabeltypedegree
i64strstri64
1"1""server"3
2"2""server"1
3"3""server"1
4"4""server"1
``` ::: ::: When the graph already has nodes, the numbering continues from them. Here the star's hub is labelled `"2"` because `"Gateway"` is node `1`, and an extra edge then links the gateway to the hub: ::: {#c82ef998 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Gateway") .add_star_graph(n=4) .add_edge("Gateway", "2") ) graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['2--3', '2--4', '2--5', 'Gateway--2'] ``` ::: :::
